item.title: Version 0.21.0
item.description:
A revision knows which episode it belongs to.
Every page of a delivery carries a label — EP 110 - "A Sheriff...Sheriff..." - YELLOW Revision - 03/10/19 — and the episode is written in it. The import reads that label, and the file name behind it, and compares it with the script it is about to be spliced into. When they disagree it says so before anything happens, in the terms a production uses: these pages are 1x10, this script is 1x08.
If that episode is in the project, it offers to import into that one instead. A season lives in one project, so the right script is usually a few rows up in the sidebar.
This is worth stopping for because nothing fails when it goes wrong. The scene numbers simply do not match, so the pages arrive as new scenes, and what you get is one script holding two episodes — which is exactly how this was found: sixteen scenes of one episode sitting at the top of another.

item.title: Version 0.20.0
item.description:
A season in one project, reports that span it, and the scene order put right.
The scripts in a project are arranged as show, season, episode. Television numbers episodes in one run — Ep104 is season 1 episode 4, 208 is season 2 episode 8 — so the season and the episode are already in the name the production sent, and they are read out of it rather than asked for again. Seasons fold away, episodes sit in episode order with their number beside the file name, and a script whose name says nothing is left alone, because a feature is not season 9 of anything.
Reports cover the episodes you choose: this one, the whole season, or a few of them. Each episode is built as it always was and the sections put together afterwards, so every one opens with its own heading — which is what tells you whose scene 12 you are looking at.
Fixed: the scene list came back in two runs, with low-numbered scenes stranded behind the end of the episode. Splicing a revision places each arriving scene after the last scene below it, and when there is nothing below it the answer is the top, not the bottom. Scene 1 arriving into a delivery that starts at 13 went behind scene 84.
Fixed: Restart Now did nothing. Sparkle stages the new version and cannot swap the bundle while the old one is running, so it hands that back and waits — and the method it waits on was empty. Anyone on 0.19.0 will need to install this one by hand; from here on the button works.
Fixed: the script jumped under the hand scrolling it. Scrolling selects the scene at the top of the window, and every change to the selection was rebuilding the entire script — a hundred scenes laid out and compared — on the main thread.
Fixed: Import Revision never opened its file panel, from the button, the menu or ⇧⌘R. Two file importers were chained on the same view, and SwiftUI presents one and silently ignores the other.
Also: a project opens on double-click. The colour of paper a scene was printed on now reads as a band across the head of the scene and a heavier bar down its edge, in the script and the scene list both, rather than a one-pixel rule nobody could find.

item.title: Version 0.19.0
item.description:
Settings, a script you can mark by hand, and two departments that should always have been there.
Settings is at ⌘, and holds the size of all three columns. The script is in points, because a screenplay is set in one face at one size and that is the number you mean. The scene list and the breakdown are in steps, because they are ordinary interface text with no single size to name. Day, Night, or whatever the system is doing — the app followed the system, and the system is dark, so it was a night app whether or not that suited the room.
The script can be marked by hand. Select any phrase, right-click, and either file it under a department or mark it. Filing it makes a finding like any other, with the words kept as its quote, so the script marks them in that department's colour and the breakdown lists it beside the model's own. A mark belongs to nobody: it is for the thing you want to come back to and cannot yet name, and it says "look here" without telling everyone else the words are a props item. Both survive a re-run, as a note does.
Doing that meant rebuilding the script pane on AppKit. A selection cannot cross two labels, and SwiftUI gives the reader a selection and the program no way to read it — there is no version of "select the tea kettle and file it under props" that could be built on what was there.
Sound and music are departments. They were left out on the grounds that they are cut after the shoot, which does not survive contact with a schedule: a jukebox has to be cleared and played on set, a radio the actors react to is playback somebody rigs, and a song named in the action is a licence bought before the day. The prompt used to say in as many words that sounds are never listed. It no longer does.
The colours follow the convention every marked-up script uses — cast green, props red, costume blue, set dressing magenta, extras cyan, stunts orange, sound yellow, music light green. Six of them were somewhere else: cast was red, which is props, and props were purple, which is set dressing. On paper that is not a different palette, it is a wrong one.
Fixed: Import Revision never opened its panel — not under automation, on any machine. Two file importers were chained on the same view and SwiftUI presents one and silently ignores the other, so the button, the menu item and ⇧⌘R all did nothing and nothing reported a problem.
Fixed: the second character's line on the Character Arc chart doubled back across the page. Scene numbers are text, so the axis is a list of categories, and left to work the order out Charts took it from the order the marks arrived in — the first character's scenes set the axis and the second character's own scenes were appended after the end of it.
Fixed: the splash stood for four seconds and then the window did not come forward at all, which is a poor first impression for the one moment the splash exists to make. It is 1.5 seconds now, 60 per cent larger, and the window crossfades in behind it.
Fixed: listing the models folder happened on the main thread, so the permission prompt that folder raises froze the entire app for as long as it stood — including the splash's own timer and the failsafe meant to rescue it.

item.title: Version 0.18.0
item.description:
What is between two characters, a window you can rearrange, and a splash that behaves.
Character Arc gained a second view. Pick exactly two characters and 'Between them' reads the relationship itself rather than showing you two arcs side by side — those are different questions, and 'she is frightened, he is calm' says nothing about whether they trust each other. A short extra pass covers only the scenes they share and asks one question of each: where these two stand, on a scale that runs from at war through neutral to inseparable, who has the upper hand, and what shifts. The scenes where it changes are marked, found by comparing each scene with the one before it in story order. A couple of minutes for a pair, and it is kept, so it only happens once.
A new version now says so in a window in front of the app rather than a thin strip along the top that nobody reads.
Any of the three columns — scenes, breakdown, script — can be put away, from the View menu at ⌃⌘1, ⌃⌘2 and ⌃⌘3. What you leave showing is remembered.
The splash has no white card. The artwork floats with a glow of its own, and it opens over the middle of the window it is standing in front of rather than the middle of the screen. The main window now waits behind it instead of arriving at the same moment.
Fixed: a saved relationship reading stored scene numbers by position, so a revision that cut a scene would have quietly turned a reading of three scenes into a reading of three different ones. Readings now follow their scenes through a revision, and say so when the script has changed under them.

item.title: Version 0.17.0
item.description:
A sample you can open straight away, corrections that stick, and the arc opened up.
A script that is already broken down now ships with the app — 30 scenes, 349 things found, every department. The script is a synthetic benchmark and the breakdown is a real saved run of it, mistakes and all, because a sample where everything is right shows you nothing about what the reviewing is for. Three scenes are taken the rest of the way and the other twenty-seven are left as the model left them. It is on the start screen next to New Project, and you can delete it like any other project.
Corrections now teach the next run. Moving something between departments, renaming it, or deleting it are three different lessons, and all three used to be thrown away. They are kept on the project — a season — so episode one teaches it the show's vocabulary and the rest get it for free. Changing something asks one skippable question about why, since the model being wrong and your production calling it something else look identical from outside. Changes (⇧⌘Y) has a second tab listing what it has learned, with a Forget beside each one. None of it leaves this Mac; the app has no way to send it anywhere.
Character Arc: the columns are yours now. It opens as a DP's view, but any department the breakdown found can be a column, and 'Only theirs' narrows them to things that name the character — so the same scenes become a costume continuity list. Up to four characters can go on it at once, each with a line on the chart and a column in the table, so the scene where one goes quiet and the other doesn't is a row you can point at. The CSV exports what is on screen.
Also: scene numbers in the rolling script are three times the size and sit under the rule, so you can find one going past. And the intensity dots now say what they are counting — 1 calm to 5 extreme, the model's reading of how hard a character is playing the scene.

item.title: Version 0.16.0
item.description:
Six things, mostly about the window.
The model picker and the Break Down button had been pushed off the toolbar into an overflow chevron. They now have the trailing edge to themselves, everything else moved to the leading side, and the windows that were unlabelled icons are in a new Script menu with a shortcut each. The default window is wide enough to show all of it.
The script pane shows the whole script in one scroll, with a marked line at each scene carrying its number, its eighths and the colour of paper it was printed on. Scroll past a marker and the breakdown follows you; pick a scene and the script scrolls to it.
There is a switch for each department above the breakdown, so you can walk a whole episode looking at nothing but the props.
A run now says what it found when it finishes — the counts, the departments, how long it took, and the parts worth a second look: scenes it found nothing in and quotes it could not trace back to the page.
Reports and prints carry a watermark, on by default. The name is read off the script you imported: distribution services stamp the recipient into the copy, and paperwork printed from that copy should say which copy it came from. You can change it or switch it off.

item.title: Version 0.15.1
item.description: The walkthrough's last page shows a code to point a phone at rather than a link.

item.title: Version 0.15.0
item.description: A board for everything pinned in a script, and pictures of one particular thing rather than a whole scene. Crash reports are written locally when something goes wrong — never sent anywhere, and they hold no part of any script.

item.title: Version 0.14.0
item.description: Finish a breakdown by hand: add what the model missed, correct what it found, write notes on scenes. Everything you change is recorded and survives a re-run. Pin reference pictures to a scene and print them as a look book — location and camera details are taken out of every image on the way in.

item.title: Version 0.13.0
item.description: Edit a breakdown by hand: add what the model missed, correct what it found, write notes on scenes. Everything you change is recorded and survives a re-run. Importing a revision now asks what should happen to notes on the scenes it changes.

item.title: Version 0.12.0
item.description: A walkthrough on first run and from the Help menu. Updates now say that the app has to restart to finish installing, and let you choose when.

item.title: Version 0.11.1
item.description: Fixes the launch check, which found updates and then reported none.
